lesson_title: The Pull That Never Lets Go: Universal Gravitation
hook_text: You are pulling the Earth upward right now — with the exact same force it uses on you. So why are you the one stuck to the floor?
clip_script: True sentence: your desk is pulling you toward it right now. So is the ocean. So is the Moon. Everything with mass tugs on everything else — that is why the law is called UNIVERSAL. You never notice, because gravity is pathetically weak: two learners sitting two metres apart attract with a twentieth of a millionth of a newton. Gravity only wakes up when a PLANET joins the handshake. And here is the strangest part: the Earth pulls you down with 588 newtons, and you pull the Earth UP with 588 newtons. Same force! The Earth just shrugs, because 588 newtons on ten-to-the-twenty-four kilograms moves nothing you could ever measure. The fading rule is torchlight: step twice as far back and the beam spreads over four times the wall. Double the distance, QUARTER the pull — never half. And the floating astronauts? Gravity up there is almost full strength. They float because they are FALLING around the planet, floor falling with them, nothing pushing on their feet. Weightless is not gravity-free. It is support-free.
visual_style: Threads of attraction linking every object in a classroom, thickening toward the Earth below; a torch beam spreading over a wall grid; then an orbiting station drawn as an endless fall that keeps missing the curved surface.
mood: Wonder with a grin — everyday scenes hiding cosmic bookkeeping.
pacing: Steady reveal, sharp myth-bust on the quarter rule, floating finish on the falling station.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and separate mass from weight forever.
